newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican separatists claim France bombings.
newsitem.headline: Corsican separatists claim France bombings.

text.p: Corsican separatists claimed responsibility on Friday for three bomb attacks on the French mainland and on their Mediterranean island, and threatened French Air Force planes at one island base.

The outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC-Canal Historique), in a statement to a Bastia radio station, said it bombed the Marseille headquarters of SNCM, the main shipping company serving the French Mediterranean island, on Thursday.
It also bombed the administrative tribunal in Limoges on the mainland on Thursday and an empty mess at the French Air Force's Solenzara base in Corsica on Wednesday.
The blasts caused damage but no injuries.
"We have shown with this symbolic act that we can hit the Solenzara base any time we want. If this base is used for repressive purposes, we will attack (planes)," the statement said.

A French newspaper revealed two months ago there were land mines around the Solenzara base, the only place in France where such measures existed. The defence ministry said afterwards the mines would be removed to avoid accidents.

Corsican separatists have claimed responsibility for several attacks against official buildings in mainland France in the past two months, including the town hall in Bordeaux where Prime Minister Alain Juppe is the mayor.
